newsitem.title: USA: U.S. April air cargo trade flat-Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. April air cargo trade flat-Tokyo-Mitsubishi.

text.p: The index of U.S. air cargo trade activity was flat in April after a 5.3 percent March rise that was the biggest in two years, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi said.
In its latest Foreign Trade Survey of air freight carriers, seaports and trucking firms, the bank said its air cargo index stood at 485.4 in April, essentially unchanged from the 485.6 March reading.
"April's relative weakness was largely a correction after a very strong showing the previous month," Michael Niemira, an economist with the bank, told Reuters.
"These patterns tend to be volatile, partly due to weather and other seasonal factors, so a huge gain in one month often is offset to some degree in the next," he said.
The April data showed relative strength in import-driven air cargo activity with exports weak.
The air cargo current-conditions export index tumbled 2.0 percent to 490.4 in April, reversing about two-thirds of March's 3.3 percent increase.
In marked contrast, the import index advanced 2.1 percent to 480.4, building on an extremely strong 7.4 percent surge in the prior month.
The April trend notwithstanding, Niemira said there may be more room for growth in exports than imports in coming months.

"International leading indicators look strong" and should contribute to demand for U.S. exports, the economist said. He added that import demand may be slowed by a scaling back of domestic retail inventories.

As a result, Niemira said, "this Summer into Fall likely will bring a slow but steady pickup in the export pace while the import numbers settle down a bit, contributing to some narrowing of trade gap later this year."
April's flat performance in the overall air cargo index was the weakest showing this year after January's 2.3 percent drop.

On the basis of an alternate presentation using diffusion indexes that also are not seasonally adjusted, the air cargo current conditions export diffusion index for April stood at 38.6 percent. This matched the April 1993 reading that was the all-time low since the survey question was broken out in 1989.

Mirroring the trend seen in the basic index, however, the import component was strong. The import diffusion index for April stood at 56.8 percent, which was its strongest April reading since that component was available in 1989.
The basic index (1989=100) is an equally-weighted composite index of current U.S. export and import air cargo activity that is not seasonally adjusted.
The April index of future U.S. air cargo business rose 0.9 percent to 555.6.
The overall index for air cargo export business fell 0.3 percent to 610.0 in April from 611.9 in the prior month. On the same basis, the index for export expectations rose 0.3 percent to 669.8.
On the import side, the import business index rose 1.9 percent to 439.0 in April from 430.7 in the prior month. The index for air cargo import expectations also increased 1.9 percent, to 441.4.
